summary.title: If You Don't Think You Need a VP of Product, VP of Marketing, Etc. — Then You Haven't Worked With a Great One
summary.one_liner: Early-stage SaaS founders should hire strong VPs across product, marketing, customer success, engineering and business development once they reach initial traction, not just VP of Sales.
takeaways: Founders between roughly $1m and $20m ARR often delay hiring VPs beyond VP of Sales, and the author argues this is a mistake.
A VP of Product is needed to manage growing customer needs and features once a company reaches enterprise scale (e.g., 1,000 customers).
A VP of Marketing should own the whole marketing function and revenue number, not just help sales, which a junior hire typically cannot do.
A VP of Customer Success can own installed-base revenue growth, churn, and processes, and should partner with the VP of Sales.
A VP of Engineering should take over repeatable work like scaling, security and devops so the CTO can focus on novel problems; the author says a mediocre hire slows things down.
summary.summary: This SaaStr opinion post argues that founders at roughly $1m to $20m ARR should hire strong VPs beyond sales, including product, marketing, customer success, engineering, business development and people. The author goes role by role, responding to common founder objections such as "my CTO is amazing" or "I have enough leads," and explains what each VP should own. The central point is that the author places the trigger for these hires at initial traction (about $1.5m ARR, when growth becomes repeatable), and that the hires only pay off if they are truly great. The page is written as personal advice and contains no tools, data or step-by-step method.
